questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The mean deviation from the mean of the series $a, a+d, a+2 d, \ldots, a+2 n d$, is
questions.solution:
The mean of the series $a, a+d, a+2 d, \ldots a+2 n d\begin{aligned}
& \text { is } \bar{x}=\frac{1}{2 n+1}[a+a+d+a+2 d+\ldots+a+2 n d] \\
& \Rightarrow \bar{x}=\frac{1}{2 n+1}\left\{\frac{2 n+1}{2}(a+a+2 n d)\right\}=a+n d
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Mean deviation from mean,
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{MD}=\frac{1}{2 n+1} \sum_{r=0}^{2 n}|(a+r d)-(a+n d)| \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \mathrm{MD}=\frac{1}{2 n+1} \sum_{r=0}^{2 n}|r-n| d \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \mathrm{MD}=\frac{1}{2 n+1}\{2 d(1+2+\ldots+n)\}=\frac{n(n+1) d}{2 n+1}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sum_{i=1}^9\left(x_i-5\right)=9$ and $\sum_{i=1}^9\left(x_i-5\right)^2=45$, then the standard deviation of the 9 items $x_1, x_2 \ldots, x_9$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, } \sum_{i=1}^{\mathcal{y}}\left(x_i-5\right)=9 \\ & \sum x_i-45=9 \Rightarrow \sum x_i=54\end{aligned}$
Also, $\sum_{i=1}^9\left(x_i-5\right)^2=45\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad & \sum x_i^2-10 \times 54+25 \times 9=45 \\ & \sum x_i^2=360\end{aligned}\therefore$ Standard deviation $(\sigma)=\sqrt{\frac{360}{9}-\left(\frac{54}{9}\right)^2}=2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sum_{i=1}^{10}\left(x_i-3\right)=7$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{10}\left(x_i-3\right)^2=27$, then the standard deviation of the 10 items
questions.solution:
We have,
$\sum_{i=1}^{10}\left(x_i-3\right)=7 \text { and } \sum_{i=1}^{10}\left(x_i-3\right)^2=27\therefore$ Standard deviation is remain unchanged, if observation are added or subtracted by a fixed number.
$\therefore$ Standard deviation
$\begin{aligned}
& =\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{10}(x i-3)^2}{10}-\left(\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{10}(x i-3)}{10}\right)^2} \\
& =\sqrt{\frac{27}{10}-\left(\frac{7}{10}\right)^2} \\
& =\sqrt{\frac{270}{100}-\frac{49}{100}}=\frac{\sqrt{221}}{10}=\frac{14.86}{10}=1.486
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The variance of first $n$ natural numbers is
questions.solution:
Variance of first $n$ natural numbers is given by
$\begin{aligned}
\text { Variance } & =\frac{\Sigma n^2}{n}-\left(\frac{\Sigma n}{n}\right)^2 \\
& =\frac{n(n+1)(2 n-1)}{6 n}-\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2 n}\right)^2 \\
& =(n+1)\left[\frac{2 n-1}{6}-\frac{(n+1)}{4}\right] \\
& =\frac{(n+1)}{12}[4 n-2-3 n-3] \\
& =\frac{(n+1)}{12} \times(n-5)
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\bar{x}_1$ and $\bar{x}_2$ are the means of two distributions such that $\bar{x}_1 \lt \bar{x}_2$ and $\bar{x}$ is the mean of the combined distribution, then
questions.solution:
Let $n_1$ and $n_2$ be the number of observations in two groups having means $\overline{X_1}$ and $\overline{X_2}$ respectively.
Then $\quad \bar{X}=\frac{n_1 \bar{X}_1+n_2 \bar{X}_2}{n_1+n_2}-\bar{X}_2$
Now, $\bar{X}-\bar{X}_1=\frac{n_1 \bar{X}_1+n_2 \bar{X}_2}{n_1+n_2}-\bar{X}_1=\frac{n_2\left(\bar{X}_2-\bar{X}_1\right)}{n_1+n_2}\gt0 \quad\left[\because \bar{X}_2\gt\bar{X}_1\right]\Rightarrow \quad \bar{X}\gt\bar{X}_1...(i)$
And $\quad \bar{X}-\bar{X}_2=\frac{n\left(\bar{X}_1-\bar{X}_2\right)}{n_1+n_2} \lt 0 \quad\left[\because \bar{X}_2\gt\bar{X}_1\right]\Rightarrow \quad \bar{X} \lt \bar{X}_2...(ii)$
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), $\bar{X}_1 \lt \bar{X} \lt \bar{X}_2$
